lines: When concept impresses in order for entry
into the nature just told — then the contemplation
sequence, preceded by true reason, true scripture
and true teacher's instruction, has its use.
sanskrit_cite: tatra yadā vikalpaṃ krameṇa saṃskurute samanantaroktasvarūpapraveśāya tadā bhāvanākramasya sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśapūrvakasya asti upayogaḥ

lines: By concept-strength alone beings take
themselves as bound; that misapprehension is
the chain that stops saṃsāra — so a counter-pair
concept arises and tears the concept that causes
saṃsāra: the cause of rising good.
sanskrit_cite: tathā hi vikalpabalāt eva jantavo baddham ātmānam abhimanyante sa abhimānaḥ saṃsārapratibandhahetuḥ ataḥ pratidvandvirūpo vikalpa uditaḥ saṃsārahetuṃ vikalpaṃ dalayati iti abhyudayahetuḥ

lines: That concept, having crossed all delimited
tattvas from Śiva to the limit, is undelimited
consciousness-merely-formed — that is the supreme
truth, where thing-ordering stands, the world's
essence; by it he breathes the world: that am I,
world-crossed — world-self am I.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca evaṃrūpaḥ samastebhyaḥ paricchinnasvabhāvebhyaḥ śivāntebhyaḥ tattvebhyo yat uttīrṇam aparicchinnasaṃvinmātrarūpaṃ tad eva ca paramārthaḥ tat vastuvyavasthāsthānaṃ tat viśvasya ojaḥ tena prāṇiti viśvam tad eva ca aham ato viśvottīrṇo viśvātmā ca aham iti

lines: This does not arise for the māyā-blind —
true-reason and the rest are absent.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca ayaṃ māyāndhānāṃ na utpadyate sattarkādīnām abhāvāt

lines: Viṣṇu-and-rest are held in scripture by
passion-tattva only, so even higher vision draws
no inclination from them — hostile to true-reason,
true scripture, true teacher's word alone.
sanskrit_cite: vaiṣṇavādyā hi tāvanmātra eva āgame rāgatattvena niyamitā iti na ūrdhvadarśane 'pi tadunmukhatāṃ bhajante tataḥ sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśadveṣiṇa eva

lines: As said in the Pārameśvara: all
Viṣṇu-and-rest are dyed with knowledge-passion.
sanskrit_cite: yathoktaṃ pārameśvare vaiṣṇavādyāḥ samastās te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ

lines: They find no supreme tattva —
devoid of the omniscient's knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: na vindanti paraṃ tattvaṃ sarvajñajñānavarjitāḥ iti

lines: Therefore only those pierced by firm
Śāṃbhava-descent, impressing concept by the order
of true scripture and the rest, enter the supreme
own-nature.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt śāṃbhavadṛḍḥaśaktipātāviddhā eva sadāgamādikrameṇa vikalpaṃ saṃskṛtya paraṃ svarūpaṃ praviśanti

lines: But then would the supreme tattva be
concept-form? Not so: the concept's work is done
merely in breaking residence-in-duality; the
supreme is everywhere all-formed, self-luminous —
no service or refutation of it for anyone.
sanskrit_cite: nanu itthaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vikalpyarūpaṃ syāt maivam vikalpasya dvaitādhivāsabhaṅgamātre caritārthatvāt paraṃ tattvaṃ tu sarvatra sarvarūpatayā svaprakāśam eva iti na tatra vikalpaḥ kasyaicit upakriyāyai khaṇḍanāyai vā

lines: There, for the excessively firm-pierced,
true-reason arises of itself, self-attained — he is
called one initiated by the goddesses.
sanskrit_cite: tatra atidṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhasya svayam eva sāṃsiddhikatayā sattarka udeti yo 'sau devībhiḥ dīkṣita iti ucyate

lines: For another, by the order of scripture —
with elaboration we will tell this in the
revelation of power-descent.
sanskrit_cite: anyasya āgamakrameṇa ityādi savistaraṃ śaktipātaprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ

lines: But the task lies in determining the
teacher's scripture, and in the fitting concept
born of the scripture's chain of kin: that chain
is true-reason; called contemplation too — from
indistinctness, an existing thing is contemplated
as non-existent by being made distinct.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ tu guror āgamanirūpaṇe vyāpāraḥ āgamasya ca niḥśaṅkasajātīyatatprabandhaprasavanibandhanasamucitavikalpodaye vyāpāraḥ tathāvidhavikalpaprabandha eva sattarka iti uktaḥ sa eva ca bhāvanā bhaṇyate asphuṭatvāt bhūtam api artham abhūtam iva sphuṭatvāpādanena bhāvyate yayā iti

lines: And here no other yoga-limb is a direct
means apart from true-reason, light-form of pure
knowledge: austerity, restraint, nonviolence, yama,
retention, prāṇāyāma — what task in consciousness
by being fixed in the knowable merely?
sanskrit_cite: na ca atra sattarkāt śuddhavidyāprakāśarūpāt ṛte anyat yogāṅgaṃ sākṣāt upāyaḥ tapaḥprabhṛteḥ niyamavargasya ahiṃsādeś ca yamaprakārasya pūrakādeḥ prāṇāyāmavargasya vedyamātraniṣṭhatvena ka iva saṃvidi vyāpāraḥ

lines: Withdrawal too should make the
instrument-level excellent; meditation,
concentration, samādhi too, successively by
practice-order, should impart identity-with-
meditated-object to the meditator.
sanskrit_cite: pratyāhāro 'pi karaṇabhūmim eva sātiśayāṃ kuryāt dhyānadhāraṇāsamādhayo 'pi yathottaram abhyāsakrameṇa nirvartyamānā dhyeyavastutādātmyaṃ dhyātuḥ vitareyuḥ

lines: But practice in the supreme tattva —
in Śiva-self, own-nature — is simply not
possible.
sanskrit_cite: abhyāsaś ca pare tattve śivātmani svasvabhāve na saṃbhavaty eva

lines: For one rooted in consciousness, practice
is the fixing of breath, mind and body — like
carrying loads, knowing scripture's meaning,
dance-practice; but in consciousness-form nothing
is taken, nothing removed — how then practice?
sanskrit_cite: saṃvidrūḍhasya prāṇabuddhidehaniṣṭhīkaraṇarūpo hi abhyāsaḥ bhārodvahanaśāstrārthabodhanṛttābhyāsavat saṃvidrūpe tu na kiṃcit ādātavyaṃ na apasaraṇīyam iti katham abhyāsaḥ

lines: If asked — 'by reasoning too?' — it is
said: this is only the mode of removing
residence-in-duality, nothing else.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ tarkeṇāpi iti cet uktam atra dvaitādhivāsanirāsaprakāra eva ayaṃ na tu anyat kiṃcid iti

lines: Even in ordinary practice: the making
of the desired form of body and the rest as
consciousness-selfhood, and the contemplation of
other forms' absence — that alone is practice's
purpose.
sanskrit_cite: laukike 'pi vā abhyāse cidātmatvena sarvarūpasya tasya tasya dehādeḥ abhimatarūpatāprakaṭīkaraṇaṃ taditararūpanyagbhāvanaṃ ca iti eṣa eva abhyāsārthaḥ

lines: In the supreme tattva: nothing there
to discard — so it is said.
sanskrit_cite: paratattve tu na kiṃcit apāsyam iti uktam

lines: Residence-in-duality too, mark well, is no
separate thing: mere own-nature-manifestation —
so its rejection is done by concept, from the
saying.
sanskrit_cite: dvaitādhivāso 'pi nāma na kaścana pṛthak vastubhūtaḥ api tu svarūpākhyātimātraṃ tat ato dvaitāpāsanaṃ vikalpena kriyata ity ukteḥ

lines: This supreme truth, own-nature shining as
manifestation-form, is taken by itself from
autonomy; by the order — thrown off, turned to
expansion, expanding, expanded — it shines; and
shining too is the Lord's own nature — so here
the yoga-limbs are not the direct means.
sanskrit_cite: ayaṃ paramārthaḥ svarūpaṃ prakāśamānam akhyātirūpatvaṃ svayaṃ svātantryāt gṛhītaṃ krameṇa projjhya vikāsonmukham atha vikasat atha vikasitam ity anena krameṇa prakāśate tathā prakāśanam api parameśvarasya svarūpam eva tasmāt na atra yogāṅgāni sākṣāt upāyaḥ

lines: Reason may favor it, but true-reason alone
is the direct means there; pure knowledge too,
impressed in many forms: offering, fire-offering,
recitation, vow, yoga. Therein all states' abode
is the Supreme Lord alone — nothing separate; for
conviction, offering all states to the Lord is
the offering — from heart-nature, offering in the
Lord is easy for those who themselves show
consciousness-entry; hence external flower,
satisfaction, scent and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: tarkaṃ tu anugṛhṇīyur api sattarka eva sākṣāt tatra upāyaḥ sa eva ca śuddhavidyā sa ca bahuprakāratayā saṃskṛto bhavati tadyathā yāgo homo japo vrataṃ yoga iti tatra bhāvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ parameśvara eva sthitiḥ nānyat vyatiriktam asti iti vikalparūḍhisiddhaye parameśvara eva sarvabhāvārpaṇaṃ yāgaḥ sa ca hṛdyatvāt ye saṃvidanupraveśaṃ svayam eva bhajante teṣāṃ suśakaṃ parameśvare arpaṇam ity abhiprāyeṇa hṛdyānāṃ kusumatarpaṇagandhādīnāṃ bahir upayoga uktaḥ

lines: All states are made of the Lord's light:
for convicted-concept-attaining, in the Lord's
consciousness-fire light, desiring to swallow all
states — sudden dissolution of all states into
mere light-residue: fire-offering.
sanskrit_cite: sarve bhāvāḥ parameśvaratejomayā iti rūḍhavikalpaprāptyai parameśasaṃvidanalatejasi samastabhāvagrāsarasikatābhimate tattejomātrāvaśeṣatvasahasamastabhāvavilāpanaṃ homaḥ

lines: Likewise, for the arising of both-natured
contemplation, by disregard alone of states
divided by outer, inner, knowable-forms: that
supreme tattva is own-nature-formed — inner
contemplation: recitation.
sanskrit_cite: tathā ubhayātmakaparāmarśodayārthaṃ bāhyābhyantarādiprameyarūpabhinnabhāvānapekṣayaiva evaṃvidhaṃ tat paraṃ tattvaṃ svasvabhāvabhūtam iti antaḥ parāmarśanaṃ japaḥ

lines: For gaining, everywhere-always, the
impersonal Lord-identification, by equality with
the Lord: viewing even the body, even a pot and
the rest — vow.
sanskrit_cite: sarvatra sarvadā nirupāyaparameśvarābhimānalābhāya parameśvarasamatābhimānena dehasyāpi ghaṭāder api avalokanaṃ vratam

lines: The Śrī-Nandiśikhā says it:
all-equality, the supreme vow.
sanskrit_cite: yathoktaṃ śrīnandiśikhāyām sarvasāmyaṃ paraṃ vratam iti

lines: Thus, by various concepts formed of pure-
knowledge portions, what concept-independent
natural supreme-truth tattva shines — for
establishment in being merely eternal-such-
shining, the specific concept tracking its own
nature: yoga.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ vicitraiḥ śuddhavidyāṃśarūpaiḥ vikalpaiḥ yat anapekṣitavikalpaṃ svābhāvikaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ prakāśate tasyaiva sanātanatathāvidhaprakāśamātratārūḍhaye tatsvarūpānusaṃdhānātmā vikalpaviśeṣo yogaḥ

lines: There the Supreme Lord, full-consciousness-
natured — fullness his power, clan, capability,
wave, heart, essence, pulsation, glory; triad,
Kālī, Karṣaṇī, Caṇḍī, Vāṇī, enjoyment, vision,
Nityā and rest — is denoted by scriptural
languages running each according to sense; by
that, by that form, let it be in meditators'
hearts.
sanskrit_cite: tatra parameśvaraḥ pūrṇasaṃvitsvabhāvaḥ pūrṇataiva asya śaktiḥ kulaṃ sāmarthyam ūrmiḥ hṛdayaṃ sāraṃ spandaḥ vibhūtiḥ trīśikā kālī karṣaṇī caṇḍī vāṇī bhogo dṛk nityā ityādibhiḥ āgamabhāṣābhiḥ tattadanvarthapravṛttābhiḥ abhidhīyate tena tena rūpeṇa dhyāyināṃ hṛdi āstām iti

lines: She shines as fullness-consciousness by the
seeing of whole-power-nature.
sanskrit_cite: sā ca samagraśaktitādarśanena pūrṇatāsaṃvit prakāśate

lines: His powers:
beyond counting.
sanskrit_cite: śaktayaś ca asya asaṃkhyeyāḥ

lines: The world itself: those are his powers —
who could teach them?
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ bahunā yat viśvaṃ tā asya śaktayaḥ tāḥ katham upadeṣṭuṃ śakyāḥ iti

lines: In three the world is completed: by which
this bears, sees, illumines up to Śiva-bearer-
limit as mere uncaricatured consciousness-form —
the Supreme Lord; that is his Śrīparā-power.
sanskrit_cite: tisṛṣu tāvat viśvaṃ samāpyate yayā idaṃ śivādidharaṇyantam avikalpyasaṃvinmātrarūpatayā bibharti ca paśyati ca bhāsayati ca parameśvaraḥ sā asya śrīparaśaktiḥ

lines: By which, like mirror or elephant and rest,
by difference-undifference: his Śrīparāparā-
power.
sanskrit_cite: yayā ca darpaṇahastyādivat bhedābhedābhyāṃ sā asya śrīparāparaśaktiḥ

lines: By which, with self distinct from one
another, by difference alone: his Śrīmadaparā-
power.
sanskrit_cite: yayā parasparaviviktātmanā bhedenaiva sā asya śrīmadaparaśaktiḥ

lines: The threefold holding of this — in self,
by embracing, tracking-nature — grasps: she is
the Goddess Śrīparā herself, named by other
words: Śrīmat-mātṛ, sat-bhāva, kāla, karṣiṇī.
sanskrit_cite: etat trividhaṃ yayā dhāraṇam ātmany eva kroḍīkāreṇa anusandhānātmanā grasate sā asya bhagavatī śrīparaiva śrīmanmātṛsadbhāvakālakarṣiṇyādiśabdāntaraniruktā

lines: Four powers, by autonomy: each runs
threefold on its own.
sanskrit_cite: tā etāḥ catasraḥ śaktayaḥ svātantryāt pratyekaṃ tridhaiva vartante

lines: Through creation, preservation,
dissolution — four by three: twelve they become.
sanskrit_cite: sṛṣṭau sthitau saṃhāre ca iti dvādaśa bhavanti

lines: Thus consciousness first constructs the
state within; then outside by distinctness;
taking reddened-nature right there; then,
intending reabsorption, forms the doubt that
obstructs it and grasps it; the doubt-portion he
constructs in self by reabsorption; then
constructs even my-this-form, reabsorber-nature,
as own-nature; then, in that construction, some
state's habit-standing, some's consciousness-
residue; then, inseparable from own-nature-
constructing, the instrument-wheel; then the
instrument-Lord; then the māyic knower-form;
then the knower contraction-release-turned,
expansion-grasping, taste-loving; therefore the
expanded form too — thus these twelve Goddess-
consciousnesses, one knower-object or several,
simultaneously or in order, two-wise, three-wise,
even-standing, arising-portioned, revolving like
a wheel, outside by month-segment-asterism
order, within by pot-cloth order too, shining,
nourishing the wheel-Lord's autonomy, denoted
by the word Śrīkālī.
sanskrit_cite: tathā hi saṃvit pūrvam antar eva bhāvaṃ kalayati tato bahir api sphuṭatayā kalayati tatraiva raktimayatāṃ gṛhītvā tataḥ tam eva bhāvam antar upasaṃjihīrṣayā kalayati tataś ca tadupasaṃhāravighnabhūtāṃ śaṅkāṃ nirmiṇoti ca grasate ca grastaśaṅkāṃśaṃ bhāvabhāgam ātmani upasaṃhāreṇa kalayati tata upasaṃhartṛtvaṃ mamedaṃ rūpam ity api svabhāvam eva kalayati tata upasaṃhartṛsvabhāvakalane kasyacid bhāvasya vāsanātmanā avasthitiṃ kasyacit tu saṃvinmātrāvaśeṣatāṃ kalayati tataḥ svarūpakalanānāntarīyakatvenaiva karaṇacakraṃ kalayati tataḥ karaṇeśvaram api kalayati tataḥ kalpitaṃ māyīyaṃ pramātṛrūpam api kalayati saṅkocatyāgonmukhavikāsagrahaṇarasikam api pramātāraṃ kalayati ato vikasitam api rūpaṃ kalayati iti etā dvādaśa bhagavatyaḥ saṃvidaḥ pramātṝn ekaṃ vāpi uddiśya yugapat krameṇa dviśaḥ triśa ityādisthityāpi udayabhāginyaḥ cakravad āvartamānā bahir api māsakalārāśyādikrameṇa antato vā ghaṭapaṭādikrameṇāpi bhāsamānāḥ cakreśvarasya svātantryaṃ puṣṇatyaḥ śrīkālīśabdavācyāḥ

lines: And construction is motion, throw,
knowledge, counting, enjoyment-making, sound,
self-dissolving too.
sanskrit_cite: kalanaṃ ca gatiḥ kṣepo jñānaṃ gaṇanaṃ bhogīkaraṇaṃ śabdanaṃ svātmalayīkaraṇaṃ ca

lines: As the Śrībhūtirāja-teachers say: from
throw and from knowledge Kālī — by subjection
to construction, then.
sanskrit_cite: yad āhuḥ śrībhūtirājaguravaḥ kṣepāj jñānāc ca kālī kalanavaśatayātha iti

lines: And this meaning: to be considered where
it stands spread in my composed commentary, in
treatise, hymn and rest.
sanskrit_cite: eṣa ca arthaḥ tatra tatra madviracite vivaraṇe prakaraṇastotrādau vitatya vīkṣyaḥ

lines: Neither too secret to show somewhere
nor hidden every way — so our teachers.
sanskrit_cite: na atirahasyam ekatra khyāpyaṃ na ca sarvathā gopyam iti hi asmadguravaḥ

lines: Thus what was said — offering,
fire-offering and rest: in this kind the
Great-Lord alone is to be thought.
sanskrit_cite: tad evam yad uktaṃ yāgahomādi tat evaṃvidhe maheśvara eva mantavyam

lines: All take Viṣṇu-to-Śiva as ground of
rejection only, of acceptance — and that false
view must be abandoned by unsurpassable yogins;
for that the knowledge-Lord's great fervour in
the hymn of experience: as it becomes, so let
him practise — not by edible-inedible, clean-
unclean discriminations, abandoning thing-
qualities, by fancy-merely-essence tormenting
the self. Purity is not a thing-form like
blueness elsewhere — from the command of
impurity on it; like gift's command in
initiation: if 'impure there' by another command
too, the same — other-command not-existing from
being overridden — if not, Śiva's-command alone
is obstructive, established by reason and by the
omniscient, unsurpassable, endless scripture —
we will say.
sanskrit_cite: sarve hi heyam eva upādeyabhūmirūpaṃ viṣṇutaḥ prabhṛti śivāntaṃ paramaśivatayā paśyanti tac ca mithyādarśanam avaśyatyājyam anuttarayogibhir iti tadartham eva vidyādhipateḥ anubhavastotre mahān saṃrambhaḥ evaṃvidhe yāgādau yogānte ca pañcake pratyekaṃ bahuprakāraṃ nirūḍhiḥ yathā yathā bhavati tathaiva ācaret na tu bhakṣyābhakṣyaśuddhyaśuddhyādivivecanayā vastudharmojjhitayā kalpanāmātrasārayā svātmā khedanīya iti uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau na hi śuddhiḥ vastuno rūpaṃ nīlatvavat anyatra tasyaiva aśuddhicodanāt dānasyeva dīkṣitatve codanātaḥ tasya tat tatra aśuddham iti cet codanāntare 'pi tulyaṃ codanāntaram asat tadbādhitatvāt iti cet na śivacodanāyā eva bādhakatvaṃ yuktisiddhaṃ sarvajñānottarādyanantāgamasiddhaṃ ca iti vakṣyāmaḥ

lines: Therefore from Vedic on, through
Pārameśvara-system, tantra, clan, Ucchuṣma and
other scriptures too — whatever restraint,
injunction, prohibition: here it is established
of no effect whatsoever.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt vaidikāt prabhṛti pārameśvarasiddhāntatantrakulocchuṣmādiśāstrokto 'pi yo niyamo vidhiḥ vā niṣedho vā so 'tra yāvad akiṃcitkara eva iti siddham

lines: Likewise said in the Śrīpūrva and rest,
spread — from the Tantrāloka it is to be
sought.
sanskrit_cite: tathaiva ca uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau vitatya tantrālokāt anveṣyam
